ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Canadian consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 16; OFAC SDN List; UN Security Council consolidated sanctions; and FINTRAC/PCMLTFA PEP and heads-of-international-organizations indicators. Enhanced due diligence required for foreign PEPs, high-net-worth ultimate beneficial owners, and any source of funds involving non-banking channels.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed limited partnership name must be in English or French, or a romanized transliteration of another language using the Latin alphabet. The name must include a legal element or suffix appropriate to an Ontario limited partnership, typically 'Limited Partnership', 'Limited', 'L.P.', or 'LP' where permitted. Accented letters available in the local script are acceptable, but non-Latin characters and non-standard symbols are not permitted in the official registry name without a translated declared name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file written submissions with the Director appointed under the Business Names Act within 30 days of the refusal, attaching a new NUANS/name search report and supporting consents from any conflicting name holder. If the rejection is based on conflict with an existing name, the applicant may obtain and file a written consent or request abandonment by the prior holder. If the administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply to the Ontario Superior Court of Justice for judicial review within the applicable limitation period, with the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery named as respondent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office in Ontario is permissible for the limited partnership register, provided the service provider maintains a physical Ontario street address where legal process can be served during normal business hours; a postal box or mailing-only address is not sufficient. The operating restaurant itself must have a separate commercial lease and physical premises with municipal zoning, food-service, health, and fire-safety compliance, irrespective of the virtual registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: below 5% annual probability of unannounced registry or tax authority inspection. Restaurant premises: above 95% expected annual probability of unannounced public-health, fire-safety, and municipal licensing inspections. Canada Revenue Agency may conduct unannounced GST/HST registration audits after the first reporting period, which triggers a moderate, fact-specific risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.7, ss. 2–6, 10; supplemented by Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.5
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CIPSPB), ServiceOntario, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration Under the Limited Partnerships Act (Form 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; no escrow account required. Capital contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and may be paid in cash, property, or services (subject to LP Act ss. 21–22).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation, as sole general partner, accepts the initial capital contribution and executes the limited partnership declaration for Hotpot Restaurant Limited Partnership; and that the registered office be established at [ServiceOntario-validated Ontario address]; and that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as designated representative and authorized officer to execute all filings, open bank accounts, and obtain business licenses; and that any one officer of the general partner be authorized severally to sign and deliver any documents, including the declaration, consents, and payments, necessary to complete formation and regulatory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario's Ontario Business Information System (OBIS) / NUANS name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a mandatory corporate name search request for the proposed limited partnership name, including the obligatory 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP' designator. Review the NUANS report for potential conflicts with existing Ontario business names and trademarks. If the name is available, reserve it for 90 days and obtain the name search report dated within 90 days of filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS report (no more than 90 days old)
Completed Ontario Name Search Request form (online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, submit a revised name search report with a new proposed name. If the objection is based on confusing similarity, file a written submission with ServiceOntario explaining the distinguishing elements or obtain the prior name holder's consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary in Ontario (external) and ServiceOntario for final acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Declaration Under the Limited Partnerships Act containing: (i) firm name; (ii) general nature of business; (iii) address of principal place of business in Ontario; (iv) full names and addresses of each general partner; (v) address of registered office for service; and (vi) statement that the partnership is limited. Ensure all general partners sign and have the declaration witnessed or notarized if required by the registry.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Declaration Under the Limited Partnerships Act
Consent from each named general partner
Name search report and reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ServiceOntario queries the declaration for missing data or witness defects, file an amended declaration within 10 business days correcting the errors. For substantive inconsistencies, resubmit the declaration with supporting affidavits from the general partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario, CIPSPB – online or mail/counter service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Declaration and the statutory filing fee to ServiceOntario, either through the online OBIS portal, by mail, or in person at an official counter. Pay the registration fee using the approved payment methods (credit card, debit, cheque). Upon acceptance, the declaration is registered and the limited partnership comes into existence. Retain the stamped copy and registration acknowledgment for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Personal identification/proof of authority for submitters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected due to fee rejection or ineligible payment, re-submit with correct payment within 30 days. If the declaration is deficient, the registry will issue a notice; cure by filing an amended declaration and paying the applicable amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Number (BN) and CRA Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the limited partnership is registered with ServiceOntario, register for a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN). Create the partnership account and immediately add applicable accounts: GST/HST (if taxable supplies exceed $30,000 CAD annually), payroll deductions (if employees will be hired), and import/export account (if condiment supply will cross borders). Ensure the BN is linked to the general partner for filing authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration because of identity mismatch, contact the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525 with supporting partnership documents. If the account type is incorrect, add or amend accounts through the CRA's My Business Account portal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Employer and Municipal Business Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (WSIB) and local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership as an employer with WSIB within 10 days of hiring employees, unless exempt. File the employer registration form and set up the workers' compensation account. Simultaneously apply to the local municipal business licensing office for a general business license and zoning clearance for the hotpot restaurant premises. Obtain a separate food premises license from the local public health unit if preparation of food is planned.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WSIB or municipal application is delayed, follow up with written correspondence and submit a request for expedited review if the restaurant opening is imminent. If a license is denied due to zoning, apply for a minor variance or special exception with the Ontario Municipal/Planning Board, or relocate the registered office to a compliant premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Municipal Public Health Unit (for food premises) and Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (for business licensing and food sector oversight)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Premises License / Restaurant Operator's Permit (issued under the Health Protection and Promotion Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.7, and O. Reg. 493/17)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Restaurant and condiment packaging operations are generally exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under the Environmental Assessment Act; however, a duck-and-cover Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) may be required for any significant air exhaust or wastewater discharge from food processing, and grease handling must comply with municipal sewer by-laws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cooking exhaust and odour must comply with O. Reg. 419/05 (Local Air Quality) applicable emission limits; wastewater discharges must meet municipal sewer-use by-law effluent limits, including fats, oils, grease (FOG) limits and pH 6-9; solid waste and used cooking oil must be tracked and disposed by licensed carriers under O. Reg. 347/90.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety plan approval and annual inspection by the local Fire Department under Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07); Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) certification for natural gas appliances, propane systems, and elevator (if any); building structural load confirmation under Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 332/12); occupancy permit from the municipal building department; workplace occupational health and safety compliance certified under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, including COVID-19 / sanitation standard and accessibility under the AODA (Customer Service Standard).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada - federal tax authority for income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export program accounts. Digital portal: CRA My Business Account () and Business Registration Online (BRO) used for Business Number (BN) and program-account activation. Ontario Ministry of Finance administers Ontario-specific taxes (e.g., Employer Health Tax), but the 8% Ontario HST component is collected by the CRA through the harmonized return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Constitute the limited partnership under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act and register it with the Ontario Business Registry (online filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership). Step 2: Apply to the CRA for a Business Number through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; the LP obtains a 9-digit BN and program accounts: RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll) if staff are employed, and RM (import/export) if condiments are exported. Step 3: The designated member (usually the general partner) completes the registration, declaring the Ontario permanent establishment, the nature of the commercial activity (ISIC 5610 full-service dining), and estimated taxable supplies. Step 4: Foreign limited partners do not require a separate GST/HST account for allocations but must have Canadian tax filing capacity and must withhold on any partnership distributions subject to Part XIII tax. Step 5: Open the GST/HST account before the first taxable supply; provide the BN to merchants, acquirers, and suppliers; register with the CBSA for export reporting (CAERS); and, where applicable, obtain a Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA) licence and CFIA export certifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - A Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes (Income Tax Act section 96): no entity-level federal or Ontario income tax is imposed; each partner is taxed on its allocated share of partnership income or loss. For GST/HST, the Excise Tax Act subsection 2(1) treats the partnership as a separate 'person' and a 'registrant', enabling the LP to charge 13% HST and claim input tax credits. Income from an Ontario permanent establishment is taxable in Ontario in the hands of partners, including non-resident partners, subject to treaty relief. The LP files an annual T5013 information return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA subsection 240(1.1), allowing a small supplier to register before exceeding the CAD 30,000 threshold. 2) ETA section 273 joint election for deemed nil-consideration supplies among closely related registrants (e.g., corporate limited partners and the LP). 3) Income Tax Act subsection 97(2) rollover election permitting tax-deferred contribution of capital property to the partnership. 4) Income Tax Act subsection 96(3) elections regarding fiscal period, accounting method, and deemed year-end on partnership reorganization. 5) Canada does not have a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is determined by legal form, treaty interpretation, and CRA administrative policy, and hybrid mismatch rules (ITA sections 94I to 94O) may deny benefits for cross-border arrangements lacking commercial substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada for the administration of the Exchange Fund Account under the Currency Act and for foreign-exchange policy; prudential banking supervision is conducted by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (Canada). FINTRAC, as the financial intelligence unit, supervises AML/CFT compliance and cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full IMF Article VIII convertibility applies; the Canadian dollar floats freely and Canada maintains no exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions. There is no regulatory approval, quota, or conversion quota for repatriating profits, paying cross-border dividends, or settling intercompany balances. Fiscal frictions are the only material hurdles: (i) a non-resident partner's share of the Ontario LP's income is Canadian-source only to the extent the LP carries on business through a Canadian permanent establishment, so the foreign-host restaurant's active earnings are generally taxable in the host jurisdiction rather than in Canada for non-resident partners; (ii) Canadian-resident partners remain taxable on worldwide income and, if the restaurant is held through a foreign corporation, a Foreign Accrual Property Income (FAPI) current inclusion may arise on passive income while distributions out of exempt surplus return tax-free under ITA section 113; (iii) Part XIII withholding at 25% (treaty-reducible) applies to Canadian-source royalties, management fees, interest, and certain partnership distributions characterized as passive Canadian-source amounts. No additional convertibility or profit-remittance licensing applies to the Canadian side.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada abolished mandatory export-proceeds surrender with the dismantling of the Foreign Exchange Control Board in 1951. There is no statutory timeline for converting export receipts into CAD, no minimum conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate foreign currency to a Canadian bank. Residual compliance duties: (i) FINTRAC EFT reports are mandatory for every cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; (ii) the CBSA B13A export declaration must accompany condiment and goods shipments leaving Canada; and (iii) GST/HST and corporate or partnership income reconciliation must be completed for repatriated foreign revenue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Limited Partnership Annual Return under the Limited Partnerships Act (Ontario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery — Ontario Business Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary of the limited partnership registration; for a 31 March registration, the return is due by 29/30 May of the same year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the 60-day window constitutes a continuing default; the Director may publish notice in the Ontario Gazette and strike the limited partnership from the registry, resulting in dissolution of the limited partnership and loss of limited-liability protection for obligations incurred after strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period; for a calendar-year period ending 31 December, the return is due by 31 May of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CRA penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500 per partner for the fiscal period, plus additional penalties for failure to provide T5013 slips; continued non-compliance may lead to enforced collection and criminal prosecution for wilful default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory solely by reason of Ontario limited partnership status. A certified independent audit becomes compulsory if required by the partnership agreement, a lender or investor covenant, or because the partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook, applying ASPE for private enterprises; IFRS is mandatory only for publicly accountable or reporting-issuer partnerships or where contractually imposed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario does not maintain a public UBO registry for limited partnerships. The annual return filed with the Ontario Director acts as the annual confirmation that the recorded general partners, limited partners, capital contributions, and registered office details are current. Any transfer of a limited partnership interest must be recorded in the partners' register at the registered office before the annual confirmation; the general partner is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of partner and contribution data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (maintained as the register of limited partners)
Register of Directors (maintained as the register of general partners)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% aggregate (15% federal general corporate rate plus 11.5% Ontario general corporate rate); the Limited Partnership is a flow-through entity, so the rate applies to resident corporate partners on their allocable share, not to the LP itself.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for restaurant operations. Eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) that are partners may claim the small business deduction: federal rate reduced to 9% and Ontario rate reduced to 3.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, producing a combined effective small business rate of 12.2%. Foreign tax credits are available to partners for foreign income taxes paid on the overseas hotpot operations. Accelerated capital cost allowance and the GST/HST input tax credit regime apply to qualifying restaurant equipment and expenditures.
